Cover: - 201 reply: deepEqual {id:1, room, title, date, start, end}; Object.keys sorted equals the six keys exactly; typeof id 'number'; next booking id 2. Extra keys in body (id: 99, extra: 'x', __proto__ via raw JSON string '{"__proto__":{"a":1},...}') ignored: reply has only the six keys and id is the server's. - Rule 1 (415 {error:'content type must be application/json'}): header missing (send body with no content-type: use request() with headers {}), 'text/plain', 'application/jsonx', 'application/json-patch+json', 'application/x-json', 'json', '' (empty header value), 'application/ json'. Accepted (not 415, expect 201 with a valid body): 'application/json', 'APPLICATION/JSON', 'Application/Json; charset=utf-8', ' \tapplication/json\t ; x=y', 'application/json;', 'application/json;charset=latin1'. Rule order: invalid content-type AND 20000-byte body → 415 (not 413); invalid content type with invalid JSON → 415. - Rule 2 (413 {error:'body too large'}): build a valid JSON object padded with spaces (whitespace is valid JSON) to exactly 10000 bytes → 201 (the booking is valid); exactly 10001 bytes → 413; measure with Buffer.byteLength. Also a body of 10001 bytes that is invalid JSON → 413 (rule 2 before 3). Multi-byte characters: a body whose UTF-8 byte length is 10001 but string length < 10000 → 413. - Rule 3 (400 {error:'body must be a JSON object'}): empty body, 'not json', 'null', '[]', '[{}]', '"str"', '42', 'true', 'false', '{', a UTF-8 BOM (bytes EF BB BF) followed by a valid object → 400. Invalid UTF-8: a Buffer of a valid object where the title contains byte 0xFF → 201 and title contains '�' (assert exact title string, e.g. 'A�B'). Leading/trailing whitespace around a valid object → 201. - Rule order: '{}' → room error (rule 4); body with bad room AND bad title → room error; good room bad title bad date → title error; ... through each rule ensure the first failing wins (rule 4 before 5 before 6 before 7 before 8 before 9 before 10). - Rule 4 room: 'aurora', 'AURORA', ' Aurora', 'Aurora ', '', missing, null, 1, ['Aurora'], 'Dawn' → 400 {error:'room must be one of Aurora, Borealis, Cosmos'}; each of 'Aurora','Borealis','Cosmos' → 201. - Rule 5 title: missing, null, 5, '', ' ', '\t\n', 81 'a's, ' '+81 a's? UTF-16 length: 40 emoji '😀' (80 code units) → 201; 41 emoji (82 code units) → 400; 81 'é' as precomposed → 400 and 80 → 201. content.content: 1 # Full spec (verbatim from user) — owner: supervisor — 2026-11-02 2 3 Constraints: Use only Node.js built-ins (no npm install). Node v22. Project's own tests must pass at the end. 4 5 Build a meeting-room booking app: an HTTP server `server.mjs` (an ES module, run as `node server.mjs`) that serves a JSON API and a browser page, and keeps its data in one JSON file. 6 7 Server 8 - At startup the server checks `PORT`, then reads the data file, then starts listening, in that order. 9 - It listens on 127.0.0.1 at the port in the `PORT` environment variable. An unset or empty `PORT` means 3000. A `PORT` that is not made only of ASCII digits 0-9, or whose value is above 65535, or a port that cannot be bound (for example because it is in use), makes the server write one line of its choice to stderr and exit with code 1. 10 - Once listening, it prints `listening on http://127.0.0.1:` followed by "\n" to stdout, where `` is the port actually bound (with `PORT=0`, the port the OS picked). This line is the only thing the server ever writes to stdout. 11 - Its data lives in the file named by the `DATA_FILE` environment variable, as JSON in a layout of your choice. An unset or empty `DATA_FILE` means `bookings.json`. A relative `DATA_FILE`, the default included, is resolved against the current working directory, not the folder of `server.mjs`. 12 - The server reads the data file once, at startup. If reading it fails with `ENOENT` (the file, or a folder on its path, does not exist), there are no bookings yet. If reading it fails in any other way (for example the path is a directory), or its content is not data in the layout this server writes (for example it is empty or not valid JSON), the server writes `cannot read data file ` followed by "\n" to stderr, where `` is the value of `DATA_FILE` as given (`bookings.json` when it is unset or empty), and exits with code 1 without listening. 13 - After startup the server's memory is the truth: changes made to the file from outside are not noticed. The server writes the data file only when a POST creates a booking or a DELETE removes one, never at startup or for any other request, and it never creates folders. 14 - Every change is saved to the data file before its reply is sent: after a restart with the same `DATA_FILE`, the bookings, and the id the next booking will get, are as before. 15 - If saving a change fails (for example because the data file's folder does not exist), the reply is 500 `internal error` and nothing changes, the next id included. Any other unexpected failure while handling a request also replies 500 `internal error`. In both cases the server keeps running. 16 - Requests that arrive at the same time give the same result as if they had been handled one at a time in some order: of several overlapping bookings sent at once while saving works, exactly one is created and every other one gets 409, and no id is given twice. 17 - Before sending any reply, the server reads the whole request body, if there is one, and discards what it does not use, so the client always receives the reply, the 413 and 415 replies included. 18 19 API 20 - The rooms are fixed: `Aurora`, `Borealis` and `Cosmos`, in that order. 21 - A booking is a JSON object with exactly the keys `id`, `room`, `title`, `date`, `start` and `end`: `id` is a number, the others are strings. The first booking gets id 1 and each new booking the next integer; an id is never reused, even after deletes and restarts. 22 - Only the parsed JSON of a reply body matters: whitespace and key order in it are free. 23 - A request's path is its request target up to the first `?` (all of it when there is no `?`). The reply is 204 with an empty body, and the booking is gone. I wrote the POST /api/bookings tests, and all 144 pass (0 fail, 0 cancelled, 0 skipped) against the current `server.mjs`. No test failed, so there are no expected-versus-actual differences to report.

I ran `node --test test/api-booking*.test.mjs`. It reported 14 suites in total, but I only read the tail of the output and didn't confirm each file's own count.

**Files created** (I did not touch `server.mjs`, `package.json`, `public/`, `.team/` or the existing helper):
- `/root/bench-runs/h4-fad7c86d/test/api-booking.test.mjs` covers the 201 reply, rules 1 to 3 (content type, size, JSON object), and the final check that failed POSTs leave the store unchanged. That check uses a fresh server and confirms ids stay consecutive.
- `/root/bench-runs/h4-fad7c86d/test/api-booking-rules.test.mjs` covers rules 4 to 10, the first-failing-rule-wins order, and the check that fields other than title are stored unchanged.
- `/root/bench-runs/h4-fad7c86d/test/helpers/booking-utils.mjs` is a new helper file of my own. It starts a server on a temp data file and removes it afterwards. It also holds `nextDate()`, so accepted cases get a different date and never overlap each other, plus the shared assertions.

Every assertion checks the exact status, the whole parsed JSON, and `content-type === 'application/json; charset=utf-8'`. Servers and temp dirs are removed after each file's tests finish.

**Deviations from your spec:**
- In the extra-keys test I assert only that `id` is a number and not 99, not that it equals a specific value. Ids 1 and 2 are asserted in the first test, and consecutive ids are checked again in the final fresh-server test.
- I left out the `'X\u0085'` title case, as you suggested.
- I added a few cases you didn't list: a 20000-byte body with valid JSON giving 413, a multi-byte body of exactly 10000 bytes giving 201, and an identical-booking 409. I also added title rejections for an array and for an object.

The spec was clear enough that I had nothing to flag.
